To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Runge--Kuttatheory is a theory of linear operators on a linear space of polynomials, the space of the elementary differentials.
the order conditions are orthogonal relations and that the elementary differentials are obtained as a recursion.
Runge--Kutter methods are orthogonal linear methods and that the order conditions are orthogonal relations from a linear recursion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the algebraic structure of the Runge--Kuttatheory, which we believe is not yet fully understood.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the linear theory is not a side issue, but rather a major part of the RK theory.
Runge--Kutte theory is now in a nut shell.
Runge--Kutka methods are linear methods with a special structure, and the theory of linear multistep methods can be applied with minor modifications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Runge--Kuttatheory has been simplified and extended considerably.

the classical Runge--Kutte theory has been extended by a recursive approach, and that the order conditions, which were originally obtained by a complicated calculation, are now given as simple orthogonal relations.
the linear theory of Runge--Kutte methods is a very useful framework for their study.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RK-methods, as well as their extensions, have a simple, elementary structure, which is easy to handle and to understand.
the orthogonal structure of the Runge--Kutter theory is a powerful tool.
the classical theory is not a collection of unrelated facts but is based on a small number of fundamental ideas.
